My observations and thoughts:
This is the first round, so I have no market data to work with yet. I know two key facts: my production cost is $1 per unit, and the maximum any customer would pay is $4.51. This means the theoretical maximum profit per unit is $3.51 (at a price of $4.51), but at that price I'd likely only capture the very top of the demand curve — potentially very few customers. Since I have no demand data at all, my goal this round should be to learn about demand while still earning reasonable profit. A good approach is to start at a moderate-to-high price to establish a baseline for high-margin demand, then adjust based on results. I should be careful not to start too low (leaving money on the table) or too high (learning little about the bulk of demand). A price in the middle-upper range gives useful information and still earns good margin. I'll pick a price that's well above cost but below the ceiling, so I can observe demand elasticity in later rounds.
